sanskrit: duryodhanas taṃ ca veda pīḍitaṃ pāṇḍavaṃ raṇe dhārayām āsa bhīmo 'pi śarīram atipīḍitam
english: Duryodhana knew that the Pāṇḍava had been wounded in the battle; yet Bhīma too held up his sorely battered body.

sanskrit: amanyata sthitaṃ hy enaṃ prahariṣyantam āhave ato na prāharat tasmai punar eva tavātmajaḥ
english: Your son thought him to be standing ready and about to strike in the fray, and for that reason he did not smite him again.

sanskrit: tato muhūrtam āśvasya duryodhanam avasthitam vegenābhyadravad rājan bhīmasenaḥ pratāpavān
english: Then, after recovering for a moment, O king, the valiant Bhīmasena rushed with great speed upon Duryodhana, who stood his ground.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ saṃprekṣya saṃrabdham amitaujasam mogham asya prahāraṃ taṃ cikīrṣur bharatarṣabha
english: Seeing him of measureless might charging in fury, O bull of the Bhāratas, your son wished to make that blow of his fall in vain.

sanskrit: avasthāne matiṃ kṛtvā putras tava mahāmanāḥ iyeṣotpatituṃ rājaṃś chalayiṣyan vṛkodaram
english: Setting his mind firmly in his stance, your high-souled son resolved to leap upward, O king, meaning to outwit Vṛkodara.

sanskrit: abudhyad bhīmasenas tad rājñas tasya cikīrṣitam athāsya samabhidrutya samutkramya ca siṃhavat
english: Bhīmasena perceived the king's intent, and so, rushing upon him and bounding forward like a lion,

sanskrit: sṛtyā vañcayato rājan punar evotpatiṣyataḥ ūrubhyāṃ prāhiṇod rājan gadāṃ vegena pāṇḍavaḥ
english: as the king deceived him by his footwork and was again about to spring up, the Pāṇḍava hurled his mace with great force at his thighs, O king.

sanskrit: sā vajraniṣpeṣasamā prahitā bhīmakarmaṇā ūrū duryodhanasyātha babhañja priyadarśanau
english: Cast by him of dreadful deeds, that mace, like the crash of a thunderbolt, shattered both the comely thighs of Duryodhana.

sanskrit: sa papāta naravyāghro vasudhām anunādayan bhagnorur bhīmasenena putras tava mahīpate
english: That tiger among men fell, making the earth resound, his thighs broken by Bhīmasena—your son, O lord of the earth.

sanskrit: vavur vātāḥ sanirghātāḥ pāṃsuvarṣaṃ papāta ca cacāla pṛthivī cāpi savṛkṣakṣupaparvatā
english: Winds blew with thunderclaps, a rain of dust fell, and the earth trembled with its trees, shrubs, and mountains.

sanskrit: tasmin nipatite vīre patyau sarvamahīkṣitām mahāsvanā punar dīptā sanirghātā bhayaṃkarī papāta colkā mahatī patite pṛthivīpatau
english: When that hero fell, the lord of all earthly kings, a great blazing meteor, loud-roaring, attended by thunderclaps and terrible to behold, fell as the master of the earth went down.

sanskrit: tathā śoṇitavarṣaṃ ca pāṃsuvarṣaṃ ca bhārata vavarṣa maghavāṃs tatra tava putre nipātite
english: So too, O Bhārata, Maghavan rained down a rain of blood and a rain of dust there, when your son was struck down.

sanskrit: yakṣāṇāṃ rākṣasānāṃ ca piśācānāṃ tathaiva ca antarikṣe mahānādaḥ śrūyate bharatarṣabha
english: A great roar of Yakṣas, of Rākṣasas, and of Piśācas as well was heard in the sky, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: tena śabdena ghoreṇa mṛgāṇām atha pakṣiṇām jajñe ghoratamaḥ śabdo bahūnāṃ sarvatodiśam
english: At that dreadful sound there arose from many beasts and birds a still more dreadful cry on every side.

sanskrit: ye tatra vājinaḥ śeṣā gajāś ca manujaiḥ saha mumucus te mahānādaṃ tava putre nipātite
english: Those horses and elephants that remained there, together with the men, let loose a mighty clamor when your son fell.

sanskrit: bherīśaṅkhamṛdaṅgānām abhavac ca svano mahān antarbhūmigataś caiva tava putre nipātite
english: And a great sound of kettledrums, conches, and tabors arose, even from beneath the earth, when your son was struck down.

sanskrit: bahupādair bahubhujaiḥ kabandhair ghoradarśanaiḥ nṛtyadbhir bhayadair vyāptā diśas tatrābhavan nṛpa
english: The quarters were then filled, O king, with headless trunks—many-footed, many-armed, fearful to behold—that danced about and spread terror.

sanskrit: dhvajavanto 'stravantaś ca śastravantas tathaiva ca prākampanta tato rājaṃs tava putre nipātite
english: Those bearing standards, those bearing missiles, and those bearing weapons all began to tremble then, O king, when your son was struck down.

sanskrit: hradāḥ kūpāś ca rudhiram udvemur nṛpasattama nadyaś ca sumahāvegāḥ pratisrotovahābhavan
english: Lakes and wells vomited forth blood, O best of kings, and rivers of mighty current began to flow backward against their streams.

sanskrit: pulliṅgā iva nāryas tu strīliṅgāḥ puruṣābhavan duryodhane tadā rājan patite tanaye tava
english: Women took on, as it were, the marks of men, and men the marks of women, when your son Duryodhana fell, O king.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā tān adbhutotpātān pāñcālāḥ pāṇḍavaiḥ saha āvignamanasaḥ sarve babhūvur bharatarṣabha
english: Beholding those wondrous portents, the Pāñcālas together with the Pāṇḍavas all became troubled in mind, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: yayur devā yathākāmaṃ gandharvāpsarasas tathā kathayanto 'dbhutaṃ yuddhaṃ sutayos tava bhārata
english: The gods departed at their pleasure, and the Gandharvas and Apsarases likewise, recounting the wondrous combat of your sons, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tathaiva siddhā rājendra tathā vātikacāraṇāḥ narasiṃhau praśaṃsantau viprajagmur yathāgatam
english: So too the Siddhas, O king of kings, and the wandering Cāraṇas, praising those two lions among men, departed each the way he had come.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca taṃ pātitaṃ tato dṛṣṭvā mahāśālam ivodgatam prahṛṣṭamanasaḥ sarve babhūvus tatra pāṇḍavāḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Seeing him laid low, like a towering sāla tree felled, all the Pāṇḍavas there became glad at heart.

sanskrit: unmattam iva mātaṅgaṃ siṃhena vinipātitam dadṛśur hṛṣṭaromāṇaḥ sarve te cāpi somakāḥ
english: Like a maddened elephant struck down by a lion they beheld him; and all those Somakas too, their hair bristling with joy, looked on.

sanskrit: tato duryodhanaṃ hatvā bhīmasenaḥ pratāpavān patitaṃ kauravendraṃ tam upagamyedam abravīt
english: Then, having struck down Duryodhana, the valiant Bhīmasena drew near to the fallen lord of the Kauravas and spoke these words:

sanskrit: gaur gaur iti purā manda draupadīm ekavāsasam yat sabhāyāṃ hasann asmāṃs tadā vadasi durmate tasyāvahāsasya phalam adya tvaṃ samavāpnuhi
english: "'Cow! Cow!'—O fool, when of old in the assembly you laughed and mocked us and Draupadī clad in a single garment, O wicked-minded one: of that mockery receive this day the fruit!"

sanskrit: evam uktvā sa vāmena padā maulim upāspṛśat śiraś ca rājasiṃhasya pādena samaloḍayat
english: Having spoken thus, with his left foot he touched the diadem, and with that foot he spurned the head of the lion among kings.

sanskrit: tathaiva krodhasaṃrakto bhīmaḥ parabalārdanaḥ punar evābravīd vākyaṃ yat tac chṛṇu narādhipa
english: And then, red with wrath, Bhīma the crusher of hostile hosts spoke once more these words; hear them, O ruler of men.

sanskrit: ye 'smān puro 'panṛtyanta punar gaur iti gaur iti tān vayaṃ pratinṛtyāmaḥ punar gaur iti gaur iti
english: "Those who once danced before us crying again and again 'Cow! Cow!'—those we now dance against, crying once more 'Cow! Cow!'"

sanskrit: nāsmākaṃ nikṛtir vahnir nākṣadyūtaṃ na vañcanā svabāhubalam āśritya prabādhāmo vayaṃ ripūn
english: "In us there is no treachery, no fire of arson, no dicing, no deceit; relying on the strength of our own arms, we crush our foes."

sanskrit: so 'vāpya vairasya parasya pāraṃ; vṛkodaraḥ prāha śanaiḥ prahasya yudhiṣṭhiraṃ keśavasṛñjayāṃś ca; dhanaṃjayaṃ mādravatīsutau ca
english: Having reached the far shore of his supreme enmity, Vṛkodara, laughing softly, spoke to Yudhiṣṭhira, to Keśava and the Sṛñjayas, to Dhanaṃjaya, and to the two sons of Mādrī:

sanskrit: rajasvalāṃ draupadīm ānayan ye; ye cāpy akurvanta sadasy avastrām tān paśyadhvaṃ pāṇḍavair dhārtarāṣṭrān; raṇe hatāṃs tapasā yājñasenyāḥ
english: "Those who dragged Draupadī in while she was in her courses, and those who in the assembly stripped her of her garment—behold those sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, slain in battle by the Pāṇḍavas through the ascetic merit of the daughter of Yajñasena!"

sanskrit: ye naḥ purā ṣaṇḍhatilān avocan; krūrā rājño dhṛtarāṣṭrasya putrāḥ te no hatāḥ sagaṇāḥ sānubandhāḥ; kāmaṃ svargaṃ narakaṃ vā vrajāmaḥ
english: "Those cruel sons of King Dhṛtarāṣṭra who once called us barren sesame seeds—they are slain by us with their followers and kin; now let us go, if it must be, to heaven or to hell."

sanskrit: punaś ca rājñaḥ patitasya bhūmau; sa tāṃ gadāṃ skandhagatāṃ nirīkṣya vāmena pādena śiraḥ pramṛdya; duryodhanaṃ naikṛtikety avocat
english: And again, as the king lay fallen on the ground, he—gazing at the mace resting on his shoulder, and crushing the head with his left foot—called Duryodhana a worker of deceit.

sanskrit: hṛṣṭena rājan kurupārthivasya; kṣudrātmanā bhīmasenena pādam dṛṣṭvā kṛtaṃ mūrdhani nābhyanandan; dharmātmānaḥ somakānāṃ prabarhāḥ
english: But when, O king, they saw the foot set upon the head of the Kuru king by the exultant, base-minded Bhīmasena, the righteous chiefs of the Somakas did not rejoice.

sanskrit: tava putraṃ tathā hatvā katthamānaṃ vṛkodaram nṛtyamānaṃ ca bahuśo dharmarājo 'bravīd idam
english: As Vṛkodara, having thus slain your son, boasted and danced about again and again, the Dharma King spoke these words:

sanskrit: mā śiro 'sya padā mardīr mā dharmas te 'tyagān mahān rājā jñātir hataś cāyaṃ naitan nyāyyaṃ tavānagha
english: "Crush not his head with your foot, lest your great righteousness pass away. He is a king and a kinsman, and now slain; this is not seemly for you, O blameless one."

sanskrit: vidhvasto 'yaṃ hatāmātyo hatabhrātā hataprajaḥ utsannapiṇḍo bhrātā ca naitan nyāyyaṃ kṛtaṃ tvayā
english: "He is undone, his counselors slain, his brothers slain, his offspring slain, his line's oblations cut off—and he is our brother; this you have done is not seemly."

sanskrit: dhārmiko bhīmaseno 'sāv ity āhus tvāṃ purā janāḥ sa kasmād bhīmasena tvaṃ rājānam adhitiṣṭhasi
english: "'This Bhīmasena is a righteous man,' so people once spoke of you. Why then, Bhīmasena, do you set your foot upon a king?"

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā duryodhanaṃ rājā kuntīputras tathāgatam netrābhyām aśrupūrṇābhyām idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Seeing Duryodhana brought to such a state, King Yudhiṣṭhira, son of Kuntī, with eyes brimming with tears spoke these words:

sanskrit: nūnam etad balavatā dhātrādiṣṭaṃ mahātmanā yad vayaṃ tvāṃ jighāṃsāmas tvaṃ cāsmān kurusattama
english: "Surely this was ordained by the mighty, high-souled Ordainer—that we should seek to slay you, and you us, O best of the Kurus."

sanskrit: ātmano hy aparādhena mahad vyasanam īdṛśam prāptavān asi yal lobhān madād bālyāc ca bhārata
english: "For through your own fault you have met with so great a calamity, born of greed, of pride, and of folly, O Bhārata."

sanskrit: ghātayitvā vayasyāṃś ca bhrātṝn atha pitṝṃs tathā putrān pautrāṃs tathācāryāṃs tato 'si nidhanaṃ gataḥ
english: "Having caused the death of your companions, your brothers, your fathers, your sons, your grandsons, and your teachers, you have come at last to your own destruction."

sanskrit: tavāparādhād asmābhir bhrātaras te mahārathāḥ nihatā jñātayaś cānye diṣṭaṃ manye duratyayam
english: "Through your fault we have slain your brothers, those great chariot-warriors, and your other kinsmen too; I deem destiny hard to overcome."

sanskrit: snuṣāś ca prasnuṣāś caiva dhṛtarāṣṭrasya vihvalāḥ garhayiṣyanti no nūnaṃ vidhavāḥ śokakarśitāḥ
english: "The daughters-in-law and granddaughters-in-law of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, distraught and widowed, wasted with grief, will surely reproach us."

sanskrit: evam uktvā suduḥkhārto niśaśvāsa sa pārthivaḥ vilalāpa ciraṃ cāpi dharmaputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Having spoken thus, that king, sore afflicted with grief, sighed deeply; and Yudhiṣṭhira, the son of Dharma, lamented long.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca adharmeṇa hataṃ dṛṣṭvā rājānaṃ mādhavottamaḥ kim abravīt tadā sūta baladevo mahābalaḥ
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: Seeing the king slain by unrighteous means, what then, O bard, did the foremost of the Mādhavas, the mighty Baladeva, say?

sanskrit: gadāyuddhaviśeṣajño gadāyuddhaviśāradaḥ kṛtavān rauhiṇeyo yat tan mamācakṣva saṃjaya
english: He who knew the finer points of mace-combat, skilled in mace-combat—the son of Rohiṇī—what he did, that recount to me, Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca śirasy abhihataṃ dṛṣṭvā bhīmasenena te sutam rāmaḥ praharatāṃ śreṣṭhaś cukrodha balavad balī
english: Saṃjaya said: Seeing your son struck on the head by Bhīmasena, Rāma, the strongest of strikers and mighty himself, blazed up in great wrath.

sanskrit: tato madhye narendrāṇām ūrdhvabāhur halāyudhaḥ kurvann ārtasvaraṃ ghoraṃ dhig dhig bhīmety uvāca ha
english: Then in the midst of the kings, the plough-wielder, raising his arms aloft and uttering a fierce cry of anguish, said: "Shame, shame upon you, Bhīma!"

sanskrit: aho dhig yad adho nābheḥ prahṛtaṃ śuddhavikrame naitad dṛṣṭaṃ gadāyuddhe kṛtavān yad vṛkodaraḥ
english: "Alas, shame, that a blow was struck below the navel in a contest of pure valor! Never has it been seen in mace-combat, this which Vṛkodara has done."

sanskrit: adho nābhyā na hantavyam iti śāstrasya niścayaḥ ayaṃ tv aśāstravin mūḍhaḥ svacchandāt saṃpravartate
english: "'One must not strike below the navel'—such is the ruling of the treatises; but this fool, ignorant of the treatises, acts after his own willful pleasure."

sanskrit: tasya tat tad bruvāṇasya roṣaḥ samabhavan mahān tato lāṅgalam udyamya bhīmam abhyadravad balī
english: As he spoke thus again and again, a great fury arose in him; then, raising his plough, the mighty one rushed upon Bhīma.

sanskrit: tasyordhvabāhoḥ sadṛśaṃ rūpam āsīn mahātmanaḥ bahudhātuvicitrasya śvetasyeva mahāgireḥ
english: With his arms raised aloft, the form of that high-souled one was like a great white mountain, gleaming with manifold mineral hues.

sanskrit: tam utpatantaṃ jagrāha keśavo vinayānataḥ bāhubhyāṃ pīnavṛttābhyāṃ prayatnād balavad balī
english: As he sprang forward, Keśava, bowed in humility yet powerful and strong, caught hold of him with effort in his round, brawny arms.

sanskrit: sitāsitau yaduvarau śuśubhāte 'dhikaṃ tataḥ nabhogatau yathā rājaṃś candrasūryau dinakṣaye
english: The two best of the Yādavas, the fair one and the dark, shone forth then exceedingly, O king, like the moon and the sun risen together in the sky at the day's end.

sanskrit: uvāca cainaṃ saṃrabdhaṃ śamayann iva keśavaḥ ātmavṛddhir mitravṛddhir mitramitrodayas tathā viparītaṃ dviṣatsv etat ṣaḍvidhā vṛddhir ātmanaḥ
english: And Keśava, as if to calm that infuriated one, said to him: "One's own increase, the increase of one's friend, and the rising of one's friend's friend—and the reverse of these among one's foes: such is the sixfold increase of one's own self."

sanskrit: ātmany api ca mitreṣu viparītaṃ yadā bhavet tadā vidyān manojyānim āśu śāntikaro bhavet
english: "When in oneself and in one's friends the contrary should come to pass, one should recognize the decline of one's purpose and quickly become a maker of peace."

sanskrit: asmākaṃ sahajaṃ mitraṃ pāṇḍavāḥ śuddhapauruṣāḥ svakāḥ pitṛṣvasuḥ putrās te parair nikṛtā bhṛśam
english: "The Pāṇḍavas, of pure manhood, are our natural friends; they are our own, the sons of our father's sister, and they have been grievously wronged by their foes."

sanskrit: pratijñāpāraṇaṃ dharmaḥ kṣatriyasyeti vettha ha suyodhanasya gadayā bhaṅktāsmy ūrū mahāhave iti pūrvaṃ pratijñātaṃ bhīmena hi sabhātale
english: "The fulfillment of a vow is the duty of a Kṣatriya—this you know. 'I shall shatter Suyodhana's thighs with my mace in the great battle'—this was vowed of old by Bhīma upon the floor of the assembly."

sanskrit: maitreyeṇābhiśaptaś ca pūrvam eva maharṣiṇā ūrū bhetsyati te bhīmo gadayeti paraṃtapa ato doṣaṃ na paśyāmi mā krudhas tvaṃ pralambahan
english: "And he was cursed long before by the great seer Maitreya: 'Bhīma shall break your thighs with his mace,' O scorcher of foes. Therefore I see no fault here; be not wroth, O slayer of Pralamba."

sanskrit: yaunair hārdaiś ca saṃbandhaiḥ saṃbaddhāḥ smeha pāṇḍavaiḥ teṣāṃ vṛddhyābhivṛddhir no mā krudhaḥ puruṣarṣabha
english: "By ties of marriage and of the heart we are bound here to the Pāṇḍavas; in their prosperity is our own prosperity. Be not wroth, O bull among men."

sanskrit: rāma uvāca dharmaḥ sucaritaḥ sadbhiḥ saha dvābhyāṃ niyacchati arthaś cātyarthalubdhasya kāmaś cātiprasaṅginaḥ
english: Rāma said: "Righteousness, well practiced by the good, keeps in check the other two—wealth in the case of one too greedy for gain, and pleasure in the case of one too much addicted to it."

sanskrit: dharmārthau dharmakāmau ca kāmārthau cāpy apīḍayan dharmārthakāmān yo 'bhyeti so 'tyantaṃ sukham aśnute
english: "He who pursues righteousness and wealth, righteousness and pleasure, pleasure and wealth—nay, righteousness, wealth, and pleasure together—without letting one injure another, attains supreme happiness."

sanskrit: tad idaṃ vyākulaṃ sarvaṃ kṛtaṃ dharmasya pīḍanāt bhīmasenena govinda kāmaṃ tvaṃ tu yathāttha mām
english: "But all this has been thrown into disorder by the injury done to righteousness by Bhīmasena, O Govinda—however much you may speak to me as you do."

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca aroṣaṇo hi dharmātmā satataṃ dharmavatsalaḥ bhavān prakhyāyate loke tasmāt saṃśāmya mā krudhaḥ
english: Vāsudeva said: "Free from anger, righteous of soul, ever cherishing righteousness—so are you renowned in the world. Therefore grow calm; be not wroth."

sanskrit: prāptaṃ kaliyugaṃ viddhi pratijñāṃ pāṇḍavasya ca ānṛṇyaṃ yātu vairasya pratijñāyāś ca pāṇḍavaḥ
english: "Know that the Kali age has come, and remember the Pāṇḍava's vow; let the Pāṇḍava be quit of his debt of enmity and of his vow alike."

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca dharmacchalam api śrutvā keśavāt sa viśāṃ pate naiva prītamanā rāmo vacanaṃ prāha saṃsadi
english: Saṃjaya said: Hearing even this quibble upon righteousness from Keśava, O lord of peoples, Rāma, his mind not at all pleased, spoke these words in the assembly:

sanskrit: hatvādharmeṇa rājānaṃ dharmātmānaṃ suyodhanam jihmayodhīti loke 'smin khyātiṃ yāsyati pāṇḍavaḥ
english: "Having slain by unrighteousness the king Suyodhana, a man of righteous soul, the Pāṇḍava will gain renown in this world as a crooked fighter."

sanskrit: duryodhano 'pi dharmātmā gatiṃ yāsyati śāśvatīm ṛjuyodhī hato rājā dhārtarāṣṭro narādhipaḥ
english: "Duryodhana too, a righteous soul, will attain the everlasting goal—a king who fought straight, slain though he was, the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, ruler of men."

sanskrit: yuddhadīkṣāṃ praviśyājau raṇayajñaṃ vitatya ca hutvātmānam amitrāgnau prāpa cāvabhṛthaṃ yaśaḥ
english: "Having entered upon the consecration of battle, having spread out the sacrifice of war, and having offered himself as oblation in the fire of his foes, he has won the glory of the final ablution."

sanskrit: ity uktvā ratham āsthāya rauhiṇeyaḥ pratāpavān śvetābhraśikharākāraḥ prayayau dvārakāṃ prati
english: Having spoken thus, the valiant son of Rohiṇī, in form like the peak of a white cloud, mounted his chariot and set out toward Dvārakā.

sanskrit: pāñcālāś ca savārṣṇeyāḥ pāṇḍavāś ca viśāṃ pate rāme dvāravatīṃ yāte nātipramanaso 'bhavan
english: And the Pāñcālas with the Vārṣṇeyas, and the Pāṇḍavas, O lord of peoples, when Rāma had departed for Dvāravatī, were not greatly pleased at heart.

sanskrit: tato yudhiṣṭhiraṃ dīnaṃ cintāparam adhomukham śokopahatasaṃkalpaṃ vāsudevo 'bravīd idam
english: Then Vāsudeva spoke these words to Yudhiṣṭhira, who was downcast, sunk in thought, his face bent low, his resolve stricken by grief:

sanskrit: dharmarāja kimarthaṃ tvam adharmam anumanyase hatabandhor yad etasya patitasya vicetasaḥ
english: "O Dharma King, why do you countenance this unrighteousness—done to this man whose kin are slain, who lies fallen and bereft of sense?"

sanskrit: duryodhanasya bhīmena mṛdyamānaṃ śiraḥ padā upaprekṣasi kasmāt tvaṃ dharmajñaḥ san narādhipa
english: "Why do you look on, knowing righteousness as you do, O ruler of men, while Duryodhana's head is crushed by Bhīma's foot?"

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca na mamaitat priyaṃ kṛṣṇa yad rājānaṃ vṛkodaraḥ padā mūrdhny aspṛśat krodhān na ca hṛṣye kulakṣaye
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: "This is not pleasing to me, Kṛṣṇa, that Vṛkodara in his wrath touched a king's head with his foot; nor do I rejoice in the ruin of our house."

sanskrit: nikṛtyā nikṛtā nityaṃ dhṛtarāṣṭrasutair vayam bahūni paruṣāṇy uktvā vanaṃ prasthāpitāḥ sma ha
english: "By deceit were we ever deceived by the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra; with many a harsh word spoken, we were sent away into the forest."

sanskrit: bhīmasenasya tad duḥkham atīva hṛdi vartate iti saṃcintya vārṣṇeya mayaitat samupekṣitam
english: "That grief of Bhīmasena's dwells exceedingly in his heart; reflecting upon this, O Vārṣṇeya, I overlooked this deed."
